hints: For the product, expand the two binomials and replace $i^2$ by $-1$.
Collect the real and imaginary terms separately, keeping all surds exact.
For the quotient, multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of $v$.
Simplify the denominator to a real number, then divide both parts of the numerator by it.
walkthrough:
Compute the product $uv$ with $u = -3\sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i}$ and $v = \sqrt{3} + 2\mathrm{i}$ using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$uv = (-3\sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i})(\sqrt{3} + 2\mathrm{i})$$
$$= (-3\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{3}) + (-3\sqrt{3})(2\mathrm{i}) + \mathrm{i}(\sqrt{3}) + 2\mathrm{i}^2$$
$$= -3(3) - 6\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i} + \sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i} + 2(-1)$$
$$= -9 - 2 - 5\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i} = -11 - 5\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$

Compute the quotient $\dfrac{u}{v}$ by multiplying numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of $v$, which is $\sqrt{3} - 2\mathrm{i}$:
$$\dfrac{u}{v} = \dfrac{-3\sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i}}{\sqrt{3} + 2\mathrm{i}} = \dfrac{(-3\sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i})(\sqrt{3} - 2\mathrm{i})}{(\sqrt{3} + 2\mathrm{i})(\sqrt{3} - 2\mathrm{i})}$$

Divide by 7 to simplify the quotient:
$$\dfrac{u}{v} = \dfrac{-7 + 7\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}}{7} = -1 + \sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$

State the exact results in $x + \mathrm{i}y$ form:
$$uv = -11 - 5\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}, \quad \dfrac{u}{v} = -1 + \sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$$

Identify the coordinates of points $A$ and $B$ in the Argand diagram:
- Point $A$ represents $u = -3\sqrt{3} + \mathrm{i}$, with coordinates $(-3\sqrt{3}, 1)$ in the second quadrant.
- Point $B$ represents $v = \sqrt{3} + 2\mathrm{i}$, with coordinates $(\sqrt{3}, 2)$ in the first quadrant.
Sketch the Argand diagram showing the real and imaginary axes, origin $O$, and points $A$ and $B$ in their respective quadrants.

Relate the angle between segments $OA$ and $OB$ to the quotient $\dfrac{u}{v}$:
$$\angle AOB = \arg\left(\dfrac{u}{v}\right)$$
From part (i), $\dfrac{u}{v} = -1 + \sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{i}$, which lies in the second quadrant since $\text{Re} = -1 < 0$ and $\text{Im} = \sqrt{3} > 0$.
